items.description:
Blasters Family Restaurant is a fully licensed restaurant at the Cape Gate Decor Centre in Brackenfell, serving breakfast, lunch and dinner in a family-oriented, cozy setting. The restaurant is tagged online as a family-style restaurant serving authentic South African cuisine, aimed at casual, family-friendly dining in the Cape Gate area, with a licence that lets diners order wine or beer alongside their meal.

It trades Monday and Sunday from 10am to 6pm, Tuesday to Thursday from 9am to 8pm, and Friday and Saturday from 9am to 10pm, giving it longer hours over the weekend for dinner service. It suits families looking for a relaxed, home-style meal in Brackenfell without booking a formal restaurant, or dropping in for a weekday breakfast before the longer weekend hours begin.

Camel Rock Restaurant is the only restaurant in the village of Scarborough, serving fresh seafood dishes to locals and visitors on Main Road. The licensed restaurant pours Cape wine alongside its line fish, seafood platters, wood-fired pizzas and gourmet burgers, in a laid-back, family-friendly setting with a relaxed, unhurried pace of service.

The restaurant describes its location as lovely and quiet, making it a spot to sit back and take in the surroundings rather than rush through a meal. It trades daily from midday to 9:30pm, closed on Tuesdays. It suits a relaxed seafood lunch or dinner on the way to or from Cape Point, away from the busier restaurants closer to the city.

Cape Union Mart at Access Park is a fashion and outdoor-gear retailer on Van Riebeeck Road in Kuils River, describing itself as the destination for outdoor enthusiasts, adventurers and everyday explorers. The store stocks high-performance apparel, footwear, camping gear and travel accessories from trusted brands including K-Way, Hi-Tec and Old Khaki.

Shoppers can outfit themselves for hiking, camping or everyday wear in one visit, rather than sourcing outdoor gear from several specialist shops. It suits families stocking up for an outdoor trip as well as individuals picking up a single item, with the Access Park branch serving shoppers from Kuils River and the surrounding northern suburbs.

Cash Crusaders Belhar is a pawnbroking and secondhand goods store inside Airport Shopping Centre, buying and selling used electronics, tools, jewellery and other secondhand items. The branch has built a following of more than 2,600 Facebook followers, describing itself as selling both brand new and secondhand quality goods while also buying pre-loved items from customers.

The store trades Monday to Friday from 9am to 6pm, Saturdays from 9am to 4pm and Sundays from 9am to 1pm. It suits Belhar shoppers looking to sell unwanted valuables for cash, or to buy secondhand electronics and tools at a lower price than new.

Columbit is a supplier of commercial meat-processing equipment and consumables, such as corks, screwcaps and capsules, to the wine, food and beverage industries, based on 7th Avenue in Kensington, Cape Town. The company was established in 1937 and has grown into a group operating in South Africa, Australia and New Zealand, now employing between 101 and 200 people.

The Columbit Group supplies both equipment and consumables, giving wine, food and beverage producers a single source for packaging materials and processing machinery. It suits wineries, food processors and beverage producers in the Western Cape looking for an established, long-running local supplier rather than importing equipment and consumables separately.

Die Weiveld Slaghuis is a butchery in Ipic Shopping Centre, Kenridge, run by a team describing themselves as passionate meat lovers dedicated to providing high-quality meat to customers. Alongside its everyday range of beef, pork, lamb and chicken, the butchery makes its own boerewors and biltong on site.

Specialities include a jalapeño and cheese wors alongside the classic beef boerewors, both sold in convenient prepacked sizes. Customers can shop in person at the Kenridge branch or place an order online for delivery. It suits households wanting quality butchery cuts and home-style boerewors and biltong without a special trip into town.

Excentric Hair Artists, trading as Excentric on Kloof, is a hair salon on Kloof Street in Gardens known among Cape Town's curly-hair community for its treatments and styling services. A colour enhancer is available to apply after lightening treatments, priced according to hair length and the amount of product needed.

The salon is open Monday to Friday from 9am to 6pm and Saturdays from 9am to 4pm, closed on Sundays, with bookings taken by phone, WhatsApp or email. A sister branch, Excentric on Point, trades from Regent Road in Sea Point on the same hours. It suits clients with curly or textured hair looking for stylists who specialise in that hair type.

Fat Harry's is a craft beer bar and restaurant on 2nd Avenue in Harfield Village, opened in February 2015 with a focus on selling its own artisan ales at reasonable prices. The industrial-chic venue offers a range of draught and bottled craft beers alongside its food menu of gourmet burgers, grills, seafood and tapas.

Outside seating and a family-friendly atmosphere make it a casual option for groups as well as couples, and the bar side of the business is as much a drawcard as the kitchen. It suits beer lovers looking for a proper range of craft ales alongside a casual pub-style meal in the southern suburbs.

Fish4Africa is a fresh fish and seafood retailer with a deli store on Victoria Road in Woodstock, part of a Cape Town-based group that has traded from its deli stores since 2005. The Woodstock Deli can be contacted directly for fresh seafood and expert advice, alongside sister deli stores in Monte Vista and Strand.

Beyond the deli counter, the brand's products are also stocked in a number of Checkers supermarkets and SuperSpars across the Western Cape, giving customers more ways to shop its range. It suits households in Woodstock wanting fresh fish and seafood with guidance from staff who know the product, rather than a self-service fridge aisle.

Gentspride Barbershop has operated on Bluegum Street in Bonteheuwel since it was founded in 2000, growing from a single pair of clippers into a professional, trade-tested barbershop with more than 25 years of experience. The shop offers standard and modern cuts, fades and scissor cuts, and also trains apprentice barbers who want to learn the trade.

Its mission has always been to provide quality service while uplifting local talent and keeping young people off the streets, showing them that barbering can be a skill, a business and a future. Built on resilience, the barbershop describes itself as more than a place to get a haircut, with a focus on giving back to the community it serves. It suits clients looking for a classic cut with a story behind the chair.

Golden River Spur is a branch of the Spur Steak Ranches family restaurant chain on the first floor of Town Square Centre in Fish Hoek, describing itself as offering a seaside Spur experience ideal for families, beachgoers and relaxed weekend outings. The restaurant trades Monday to Thursday from 9am to 9pm, Friday and Saturday until 10pm, and Sunday and public holidays until 8pm.

Customers can dine in, sit down or take away, and orders can also be placed through the Spur app, by phone for collection, or through Mr Delivery for home delivery. It suits Fish Hoek families wanting the familiar Spur menu of steaks, ribs, burgers and kids' meals close to the beach.

Hangberg Dreams is a non-profit organisation based at St Simons on Karbonkel Road in Hangberg, Hout Bay, established in 2019 to support recovery from substance misuse and related problems. The organisation provides treatment, support and resources aimed at improving the wellbeing of individuals, families, schools, workplaces and communities through its programmes.

Its programme offering includes therapeutic group sessions, yoga and fitness, outreach work, and seasonal giving around Christmas and Easter, alongside dedicated activities for seniors. The organisation can be reached through its hotline or by email, and its staff office is open on weekdays. It suits families and individuals in Hangberg and Hout Bay looking for local, community-based support around substance misuse recovery.

Harvest Moon Watercolours is a small Cape Town business based at Imhoff Farm in Kommetjie, handcrafting 100% vegan watercolour paints from ethically sourced, cruelty-free pigments. The range includes individual watercolours in half pans, matte and pearlescent finishes, along with half-pan sets, button sets, ceramic palettes and dot cards for testing colours before buying.

The business also sells supplies such as storage tins, paper and glass droppers for watercolour painting, plus limited-edition colours and gift vouchers. Workshops are available for those who want to learn the craft in person. It suits artists and hobbyists looking for cruelty-free, locally handcrafted watercolours rather than mass-produced paint sets.

Hassans Colorado Service Station is a Shell-branded fuel station on Highlands Drive in Weltevreden Valley, Mitchells Plain, selling Shell V-Power 95, V-Power Diesel and Unleaded 93 around the clock. The forecourt is listed as unmanned, with euroShell and Shell fuel cards accepted alongside standard payment methods, so regular fleet and card customers can fill up without needing cash on hand.

Facilities on site include an ATM, disabled-access facilities and designated service bays, next to the station's convenience store for a quick snack or drink while the car is being filled. It trades 24 hours a day, every day of the week, including public holidays. It suits motorists in Mitchells Plain needing fuel, a quick stop at the ATM or convenience shopping at any hour of the day or night.

IV Bar Westlake is an intravenous vitamin drip and wellness bar in Westlake Shopping Centre, offering nurse-administered IV therapy for hydration, immunity, energy and recovery. The drip menu covers classic options such as alpha lipoic acid, biotin, glutamine and anti-inflammatory formulas, alongside more targeted drips for detox, energy boost, fertility, immune support and menopause.

Other options include a jet lag and hangover recovery drip, aimed at travellers and anyone needing a quick reset. Treatments are designed to be customised to each client's needs rather than offered as a single standard formula. It suits anyone in the Westlake area looking for a supervised vitamin boost rather than an over-the-counter supplement.

Kiki is a lively Greek restaurant on Regent Road in Sea Point, serving contemporary mezze-style sharing plates, salads and skewers with a modern twist on classic Athens and Greek riviera flavours. The whitewashed walls, blue-glazed tiles, terracotta pots and candle-lit tables are designed to conjure up a homely Greek taverna, overlaid with a more contemporary, comfortable finish.

The bar adds a range of creative cocktails to the mix, helping the venue build its own buzz on Regent Road beyond the food. It is a sister restaurant to Ariel, which does the same for Italian food nearby. It suits a lively dinner built around sharing plates and cocktails rather than a traditional sit-down three-course meal.

Kleinsky's Delicatessen is a Cape Town deli and bakery on Regent Road in Sea Point, serving bagels, breakfasts and a range of New York-style classics such as hot pastrami on rye and matzo ball soup. The business opened in 2014 as a small, hole-in-the-wall eatery, inspired by the delis of New York and Montreal and built on traditional, time-honoured recipes.

It quickly outgrew its original premises and moved across the road to its current Regent Road address, later expanding to a second location at Workshop17 on Kloof Street. The bagels are hand-rolled and slow-fermented in the classic style. It suits anyone craving an authentic deli breakfast or lunch with a Jewish-New-York flavour in Sea Point.

Lily's is a neighbourhood eatery on the Mouille Point Promenade, looking out over the Atlantic Ocean with indoor and outdoor seating that opens onto the promenade. The restaurant describes its style as comfortably refined with a quirky, esoteric edge, serving breakfast, lunch and dinner from a varied and adventurous menu.

Lily's is part of the Kove Collection group of restaurants and bars, and the venue positions itself as one of Cape Town's favourite local spots rather than a special-occasion-only destination. Its friendly, fashionable atmosphere is designed to suit a casual weekday meal as much as a weekend outing. It suits anyone wanting an all-day meal with a sea view on the Mouille Point strip.

items.description:
John's Touch Hair and Beauty Salon is a hairdressing salon on Saint Peter's Road in Mowbray, offering a broad range of hair services from balayage and colouring to curly-hair care, braiding, keratin treatments, locs, perms and permanent hair straightening. The salon also caters for children's haircuts and wig installations, alongside women's haircuts and styling, giving clients a single stop for most hair-related needs.

Trading seven days a week, the salon is open Monday to Friday from 9am to 6pm and on Saturdays and Sundays from 10am to 5pm, making it accessible for weekday appointments as well as weekend visits. It suits clients across Mowbray and the surrounding southern suburbs looking for a salon with a wide service menu, from everyday cuts to more specialised treatments such as keratin smoothing or curly-hair styling, without needing to visit several different salons.
